summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of COPD, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for acute abdominal pain and distension. She had a two-week history of constipation and presented with nausea, vomiting, and inability to pass stool. Imaging revealed a small bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum within a ventral hernia. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control after refusing nasogastric tube placement. During admission, she developed worsening respiratory status with hypercapnia, likely due to COPD exacerbation, and was treated with IV steroids without BiPAP due to her refusal and risk of vomiting. Her abdominal symptoms resolved, she tolerated a diet, and was discharged to extended care. Her lisinopril was uptitrated for hypertension, torsemide was restarted at a lower dose, and follow-up was arranged for hernia monitoring, insulin titration, anticoagulation evaluation, and possible BiPAP use.
